title: Anesthetist Salary: Hourly to Annual, Casual Loading, and Super Paid on Top
description: Understand anesthetist salary in Australia: hourly to annual conversion, casual loading, super, and tax. Compare ATO, ABS, and public hospital pay scales.
salarySummary: Full-time anaesthetists earn a median of $8,293 per week ($218 per hour) based on 46 hours, but the standard 38-hour week yields about $7,030 per week at the same hourly rate.

faqs.q: What is the typical anesthetist salary in Australia?
faqs.a: According to the Australian Taxation Office, the median taxable income for anaesthetists in 2023–24 was $457,287, while the average was $475,455. Jobs and Skills Australia reports median full-time weekly earnings of $8,293 ($218 per hour) based on a 46-hour week. Public hospital staff specialists earn less, with NSW year‑1 base salary plus allowance at $231,962 and Victoria year‑1 at $262,099.

faqs.q: How does casual loading apply to anesthetist salary calculations?
faqs.a: Casual loading of 25% applies to award‑free employees under the National Minimum Wage, but most anaesthetists are employed under awards or enterprise agreements that set higher rates. The calculator on this site lets you add 25% casual loading to any base hourly rate, which is useful for casual workers in other occupations. For anaesthetists, the loading is not typically relevant, but the feature helps compare hourly rates across employment types.

faqs.q: Is superannuation paid on top of an anesthetist's salary?
faqs.a: Yes, super guarantee of 12% of ordinary earnings is paid on top of salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). For anaesthetists earning well above that cap, super is limited to 12% of the base amount. The calculator estimates super on ordinary earnings only, stopping at the cap. For example, on a $457,287 salary, super would be about $32,500 (12% of $270,830) rather than 12% of the full salary.

bodyMarkdown:
## Anesthetist Salary: What You Need to Know

If you're researching an **anesthetist salary** in Australia, you'll find a wide range of figures depending on the source and the employment setting. This article explains how to convert an hourly rate to annual pay, how casual loading and super work, and what the latest official data shows. Use the [timesheet](/) on this site to calculate your own figures by entering an hourly rate and selecting casual loading if applicable.

### How Hourly to Annual Conversion Works

The standard formula is: **annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full‑time employee working 38 ordinary hours per week, that's hourly × 38 × 52. The calculator on this site uses this formula and assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It also adds 12% super on top of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for 38 hours, giving $1,004.90 per week and $52,254.80 per year. With 25% casual loading, the rate becomes $33.05 per hour, or $65,318.50 per year. Super at 12% on the ordinary earnings (before loading) would add about $6,270.58, but the calculator applies super on the total ordinary earnings including loading? Actually, super is paid on ordinary time earnings, which for casuals includes the loading. The calculator handles this automatically.

### Anesthetist Salary from Official Sources

Jobs and Skills Australia (JSA) reports that anaesthetists (ANZSCO 2532) have median full‑time weekly earnings of $8,293 and median hourly earnings of $218. However, this is based on an average of 46 hours per week, not the standard 38. If you apply the same hourly rate to a 38‑hour week, the weekly figure would be about $8,284 (218 × 38), which is very close to the JSA median because the hourly rate already reflects the longer hours. The JSA data also shows that 90% of anaesthetists work full‑time.

The Australian Taxation Office's latest figures (2023–24) show a median taxable income of $457,287 and an average of $475,455 across 3,735 anaesthetists. These figures include part‑time workers and those in private practice, so they are not directly comparable to a full‑time salary. The median salary or wages component was $235,037, reflecting employed anaesthetists.

Public hospital staff specialists are paid under state enterprise agreements. For example, a NSW staff specialist in year 1 earns a base salary of $197,583 plus a 17.4% special allowance, totalling $231,962. In Victoria, a year‑1 specialist earns $262,099. Queensland pays staff specialists at L18–L24 with a 50% attraction and retention allowance on top of base salary.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

The angle of this article is that **casual loading of 25% and super are paid on top** of the base rate. For award‑free employees, the National Minimum Wage order sets a casual loading of 25%. Most anaesthetists are not casual employees, but the calculator's checkbox allows you to add casual loading to any hourly rate for comparison. Super guarantee of 12% is paid on ordinary earnings, and for high‑income earners like anaesthetists, the maximum contribution base limits the super amount. For example, on a $457,287 salary, super would be capped at 12% of $270,830 = $32,499.60, not 12% of the full salary.

### Take‑Home Pay Estimates

Using the on‑site tax rates for 2026–27 (tax‑free threshold $18,200, then 15%, 30%, 37%, 45%; Medicare 2%), a full‑time employee earning the JSA median of $8,293 per week ($431,236 per year) would have a take‑home pay of about $262,685 per year, or $10,103 per fortnight, after income tax and Medicare. That's assuming no HELP debt or salary packaging. For the ATO median taxable income of $457,287, take‑home is about $276,492 per year ($10,634 per fortnight). These estimates are from the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Using the Calculator for Your Own Rate

To see how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures with tax and super, visit the [timesheet](/) and enter your rate. If you are a casual worker, check the casual loading box to add 25%. Remember that the calculator assumes a consistent 38‑hour week unless you change the hours field. For anaesthetists working longer hours, adjust the weekly hours to match your roster.

For more detailed pay guides and award rates, see the [pay guides](/blog) page. The [reference tables](/data) include the National Minimum Wage, ABS Average Weekly Earnings, and tax tables.
